title: Vendor onboarding: copy tests and acceptance gates
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures the minimal acceptance gates, copy variants, light QA tests, and risk matrix for new vendor/partner listings on cloud marketplaces (AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, GCP Marketplace). It's intended for cross-functional review between GTM, Legal, and Eng-integration before we create formal listing artifacts.

Intended audience:
- GTM (marketplace ops, partner marketing)
- Solutions engineering (partner integration owner)
- Legal/security reviewers
- Product/PM for SKU mapping and feature callouts

High-level objectives (what success looks like):
- Produce 2 short copy variants and 1 long-form description that pass legal and marketplace content guidelines.
- Validate acceptance gate checklist so listings can be turned on with minimal rework.
- Define smoke QA tests for integration (billing SKU, provisioning link, API key flow).
- Capture edge-case risks and mitigation steps.

Quick notes/choosing approach:
- Prioritize conservative copy that highlights Redwood Inference’s "inference-first" value (latency, dedicated capacity, private deployments). Avoid comparative or unverified claims.
- Keep the customer benefit language concrete (e.g., "predictable throughput for production LLM apps") rather than marketing hyperbole.

Acceptance gates checklist (MUST pass before submit):
1) Legal & Compliance:
   - Plain-language data residency statement present and accurate for target region(s).
   - No unsupported claims about SLA levels that differ from contract.
   - Export control & sanctioned countries list reviewed.
   - Contact/POC for enterprise sales included.
2) Technical / Integration:
   - Provisioning flow validated: "Subscribe" -> SAML/OAuth or license-token exchange documented.
   - Billing SKU mapped and test invoice generated under sandbox account.
   - Test account can hit the hosted API with sample keys and get valid token/response.
   - Deployment/private option references (if applicable) link to partner onboarding doc.
3) Security:
   - TLS and Minimum API security posture declared (TLS 1.2+).
   - KMS/HSM capability described for Private deployments.
4) Copy & Content:
   - Short blurb (<= 160 chars) exists and a second alternative variant exists.
   - Long description (300–700 words) draft completed.
   - Feature bullets (3–6) with clear benefit statements.
   - Logos/brand assets present and approved.
5) Marketplace-specific:
   - SKU meets marketplace naming rules and character limits.
   - Required metadata (support email, privacy policy URL, legal entity) filled.
   - Required images/screenshots uploaded (1024x1024 icon + 2–3 hero images).

Copy variants (working drafts)
A) Short (searchable blurb, 150 chars):
"Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM inference: low-latency hosted API, reserved GPU capacity, and private deploys for regulated apps."

B) Short alternative (emphasis on economics):
"High-throughput LLM serving that cuts per-token cost with smart batching and caching. Hosted, dedicated, or private deployments."

C) Long description (working draft; ~420 words):
"Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform that makes high-performance LLM inference predictable and economical. Ship features faster with a single API that runs in hosted mode for rapid onboarding, reserved capacity for predictable throughput, or private deployments for regulated workloads.

Our serving runtime includes GPU-optimized kernels, automatic KV/prefix caching, and workload-aware batching so teams can reduce per-token cost while meeting strict latency SLOs. Use the Redwood Console to track token-level cost, per-route latency, and rollout health; set canary rollouts and A/B tests with automatic failover.

Choose from a catalog of curated models or bring your own weights. For enterprise needs we support dedicated GPU pools, VPC/private control plane deployments, and integrations with KMS/HSM for key management. Security and observability are first-class: audit logs, role-based access controls, and tracing hooks are available out-of-the-box.

Whether you’re an AI-native startup or a regulated enterprise, Redwood lets engineering teams focus on building product experiences, not managing inference infrastructure. Start with a free trial of the hosted API or contact sales for reserved capacity and private deployment options."

Feature bullets (finalize 3–6):
- Low-latency hosted API with streaming and function-calling
- Reserved GPU capacity with SLA-backed throughput
- Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM support
- Smart batching & KV caching to lower per-token costs
- Console for cost/latency analytics and rollout control

Marketplace QA smoke tests (minimal reproducible set)
- Test 1: Subscribe -> Receive license token -> Call /v1/generate with sample prompt (verify status 200 and token usage header).
- Test 2: Billing validation -> Create sandbox purchase -> Generate invoice PDF -> Confirm SKU and price line match expectation.
- Test 3: Provisioning links -> Click "Get started" flows to docs with correct region-specific links.
- Test 4: Private deploy claim -> Verify KMS integration doc link opens and contains example KMS provider config.
- Test 5: Image assets -> Upload icon and hero image -> Verify file size and dimension checks.

Risk matrix (quick):
- Risk: Marketplace rejects claim about SLA.
  Mitigation: Replace specific SLA numbers with "SLA-backed options available for reserved capacity" and point to contact.
- Risk: Billing SKU mismatch causes invoice issues.
  Mitigation: Preflight test purchases in sandbox; reconcile with Finance.
- Risk: Copy contains comparative language flagged by marketplace.
  Mitigation: Run copy through legal quick-check list and prefer factual statements.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we disclose token-based pricing in listing or link to pricing page? (Product + Finance)
- Which single screenshot best demonstrates Console value for initial listing? (Design + Product)
- Is the short blurb above acceptable for EU marketplaces given data residency statements? (Legal)

Next steps (action owners):
- Ethan: Run billing sandbox purchase tests by 2025-01-20 and attach invoice sample to this doc.
- María: Finalize hero image and create 2 variants (2025-01-17).
- Ravi: Legal quick-check of long copy and data residency sentence (2025-01-15).
- Priya: Draft final marketplace metadata sheet (SKU names, support contact, privacy URL) and iterate with Finance (2025-01-22).

Notes for submitter (concise checklist to paste into marketplace UI):
- [ ] Short blurb (final)
- [ ] Long description (final)
- [ ] Feature bullets
- [ ] Logos & screenshots uploaded
- [ ] Billing SKU mapped and test invoice attached
- [ ] Security statements present
- [ ] Legal review complete
